name: Hanafuda (花札)
description: Hanafuda (花札, 'flower cards') are traditional Japanese playing cards comprising a 48-card deck divided into 12 suits, each representing a month and featuring a specific flower or plant. Hanafuda is not a single game but a family of games, most commonly fishing/capture games where players match cards from their hand with cards on the field. Popular games include Koi-Koi, Hachi-Hachi, and Hana-Awase. Cards are categorized as Brights, Animals, Ribbons, and Plains, with varying point values.

content.text: Hanafuda (花札, 'flower cards') are traditional Japanese playing cards comprising a 48-card deck divided into 12 suits, each representing a month and featuring a specific flower or plant. Hanafuda is not a single game but a family of games, most commonly fishing/capture games where players match cards from their hand with cards on the field. Popular games include Koi-Koi, Hachi-Hachi, and Hana-Awase. Cards are categorized as Brights, Animals, Ribbons, and Plains, with varying point values.
Hanafuda cards originated in 18th-century Japan, evolving from Portuguese playing cards. The Japanese government banned Western-style cards, leading to the development of Hanafuda as a workaround.
2 to 6 players depending on the specific Hanafuda game (e.g. Koi-Koi typically 2).

48 cards divided into 12 suits (months):
- January (Pine), February (Plum), March (Cherry), April (Wisteria), May (Iris), June (Peony), July (Bush Clover), August (Pampas Grass), September (Chrysanthemum), October (Maple), November (Willow), December (Paulownia).

Each suit has 4 cards, categorized as:
- **Brights** (20 points): Special high-value cards.
- **Animals** (10 points): Cards featuring animals.
- **Ribbons** (5 points): Cards with ribbons or poetry.
- **Plains/Chaff** (1 point): Simple flower cards.
Varies by game; typically dealer distributes cards to hands and table.
